source_caption:
For years, it looked like Martin Scorsese’s The Irishman might never get made.

Scorsese had spent years trying to bring the story to the screen, but traditional studios became increasingly hesitant as the budget grew. The biggest problem was the story itself: the film follows Frank Sheeran, a real-life Mafia hitman played by Robert De Niro, across several decades of his life. Scorsese wanted De Niro, Al Pacino and Joe Pesci to play their characters at different ages, which meant developing expensive new de-aging technology.

At one point, the project was expected to cost around $100 million, but the budget eventually climbed to around $160 million or more. Paramount and other traditional backers ultimately stepped away.

Then Netflix stepped in.

Ted Sarandos backed the film with an estimated $160 million budget and gave Scorsese the freedom to make the movie he wanted.

The story follows Frank Sheeran as he looks back on his life in organized crime, his relationship with crime boss Russell Bufalino, and his complicated friendship with powerful labor leader Jimmy Hoffa. The film gradually becomes less about the violence and more about the choices Frank made and the people he lost along the way.

Behind the scenes, Industrial Light & Magic spent around two years developing the de-aging technology. They even recreated a scene from GoodFellas with De Niro to prove the technology could make him look decades younger. The entire process took roughly four years.

source_details.synopsis: The Irishman (also known as I Heard You Paint Houses) is a 2019 American epic gangster film directed and produced by Martin Scorsese from a screenplay by Steven Zaillian, based on the 2004 book I Heard You Paint Houses by Charles Brandt. It stars Robert De Niro, Al Pacino, and Joe Pesci, with Ray Romano, Bobby Cannavale, Anna Paquin, Stephen Graham, Stephanie Kurtzuba, Jesse Plemons, and Harvey Keitel in supporting roles. The biographical film follows Frank Sheeran (De Niro), a truck driver who becomes a hitman involved with mobster Russell Bufalino (Pesci) and his crime family before later working for Jimmy Hoffa (Pacino), a powerful Teamster.
